title: Tally Legitimate Piece Move Tuples
content:
Picture an `8 x 8` chessboard holding `n` pieces (rooks, queens, or bishops). You are handed a string array `pieces` of length `n`, where `pieces[i]` says what type (rook, queen, or bishop) the `ith` piece is. Alongside this, you receive a 2D integer array `positions` also of length `n`, where `positions[i] = [ri, ci]` shows that the `ith` piece presently sits at the **1-based** coordinate `(ri, ci)` on the chessboard.

When scheduling a **move** for a piece, you pick a **destination** square that the piece will head toward and halt on.

*   A rook can solely move **horizontally or vertically** from `(r, c)` toward `(r+1, c)`, `(r-1, c)`, `(r, c+1)`, or `(r, c-1)`.
*   A queen can solely move **horizontally, vertically, or diagonally** from `(r, c)` toward `(r+1, c)`, `(r-1, c)`, `(r, c+1)`, `(r, c-1)`, `(r+1, c+1)`, `(r+1, c-1)`, `(r-1, c+1)`, `(r-1, c-1)`.
*   A bishop can solely move **diagonally** from `(r, c)` toward `(r+1, c+1)`, `(r+1, c-1)`, `(r-1, c+1)`, `(r-1, c-1)`.

Every piece on the board must perform a **move** at the same time. A **move combination** is the full collection of **moves** chosen for all the pieces. Each second, any piece not yet at its destination advances **one square** instantaneously toward it. All pieces start advancing at second `0`. A move combination is **invalid** whenever, at any moment, **two or more** pieces share a square.

Return _the quantity of **valid** move combinations_​​​​​.

**Notes:**

*   **No two pieces** start on the **same** square.
*   A piece's **destination** may be the square it currently sits on.
*   When two pieces are **directly adjacent**, they may **move past each other** and trade places within a single second; this remains valid.

**Example 1:**

**Input:** pieces = \[ "rook "\], positions = \[\[1,1\]\]
**Output:** 15
**Explanation:** The image above shows the possible squares the piece can move to.

**Example 2:**

**Input:** pieces = \[ "queen "\], positions = \[\[1,1\]\]
**Output:** 22
**Explanation:** The image above shows the possible squares the piece can move to.

**Example 3:**

**Input:** pieces = \[ "bishop "\], positions = \[\[4,3\]\]
**Output:** 12
**Explanation:** The image above shows the possible squares the piece can move to.

**Constraints:**

*   `n == pieces.length`
*   `n == positions.length`
*   `1 <= n <= 4`
*   `pieces` only contains the strings `"rook "`, `"queen "`, and `"bishop "`.
*   There will be at most one queen on the chessboard.
*   `1 <= xi, yi <= 8`
*   Each `positions[i]` is distinct.
